scenes.name: Sugar Hill Records y Rapper’s Delight
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Sylvia Robinson, la «madre del hip hop», venía del R&B: Little Sylvia, el dúo Mickey & Sylvia («Love Is Strange», 1956), la producción del «It’s Gonna Work Out Fine» de Ike & Tina, el sello All Platinum con su marido Joe (con supuestos lazos mafiosos) y su propio éxito «Pillow Talk» (1973). Arruinada, vio a Lovebug Starski en Harlem World en 1979 y quiso grabar aquello; con Morris Levy fundaron Sugar Hill. Su hijo la llevó a una pizzería de Nueva Jersey donde Big Bank Hank, mánager de los Cold Crush, hizo una audición en su coche junto a Master Gee y Wonder Mike: la Sugarhill Gang. Sobre una recreación de «Good Times» de Chic grabaron quince minutos de rimas que una radio de St. Louis, WESL, se atrevió a poner: «Rapper’s Delight» inundó el mundo en otoño de 1979, dejó en anécdota el «King Tim III» de Fatback y demostró que el hip hop era negocio. En el Bronx sonaba a imitación higienizada: Hank rapeaba las rimas de Grandmaster Caz («I’m the C-A-S-AN, the O-V-A»), un estribillo de Hollywood y una frase de Rahiem; «hizo retroceder el hip hop cinco años» (Charlie Chase). Para Kool Moe Dee, sin Sugar Hill quizá no habría industria. La casa no pagaba bien a sus artistas, y su banda (Skip Alexander, Doug Wimbish, Duke Bootee) tocaba los temas. En Harlem, Bobby Robinson y su sello Enjoy ficharon a Flash, los Funky 4 + 1 y los Treacherous Three.

podcast.title: Financier of Hip-Hop Venture
podcast.body: Joe Robinson's "gangster friend Morris Levy" provided financing for Sylvia Robinson's venture into hip-hop, which led to her significant role in the genre in 1979. "with financing from our husbands gangster friend Maris Lovie."

podcast.title: Gangster Connections and Manager Role
podcast.body: Joe Robinson, Sylvia Van Topoele's boyfriend, had connections with gangsters. He decided to become Sylvia's manager, believing he could boost her floundering career. "Joe Robinson was involved in some way with gangsters. Nobody has written enough detail for me to get an exact sense of what it was he did with the mob, but he had connections, and he decided he was going to become Sylvia's manager."

podcast.title: Managerial Idea for Duo
podcast.body: Some sources suggest that the idea for Sylvia to form a duo with Mickey Baker was Joe Robinson's, inspired by the success of other vocal duos like Jean and Junis. "Some sources say that the duo was Joe Robinson's idea, and that it was inspired by the success of Jean and Junis, Sheldon Lee and the other vocal duo's around the time."
